corridors.name: Clairemont Avenue
corridors.today: 4 travel lanes, no bike facility, 35 mph
corridors.proposal: Road diet to 2 lanes + center turn lane. Year 1: 5-ft bike lanes with 2-ft buffer and flex posts in existing pavement (the Safety Action Plan's near-term option). Later: curb-separated one-way cycle tracks.
corridors.impactNote: 19,300 vehicles/day is within the FHWA range where 4-to-3 conversions keep similar capacity, because the turn lane removes left-turn blockages. Needs a GDOT traffic operations study.
corridors.serves: Clairemont ES, Westchester ES (via Scott Blvd), downtown, Church St cycle track
corridors.city: Recommends evaluating a road diet. Near term: unprotected 5-ft bike lanes with a center turn lane. Later: a buffered cycle track. Not funded or scheduled. The 2026 quick-build only restripes the downtown block at E Ponce.
corridors.change: Adds flex-post protection from day one and moves the corridor into Phase 1. Ties the Scott Blvd end to the RAISE study.

corridors.name: Church Street (downtown)
corridors.ext: Commerce Dr to E Ponce de Leon Ave
corridors.today: 5 lanes (2 each way + turn lane), bike lanes end at Commerce
corridors.proposal: Back the city's 2026 quick-build Scenario 2: one lane each way, parking-protected bike lanes, barriers where parking is not possible, raised mid-block crossing.
corridors.impactNote: The block is short, with signals at both ends. Scenario 2 adds 9-11 parking spaces. Short blocks downtown are limited by the signals, not the number of lanes.
corridors.serves: Decatur Square, MARTA, library, Church St cycle track to Suburban Plaza
corridors.city: Two options: Scenario 1, barrier-protected lanes with a center turn lane; Scenario 2, parking-protected lanes, no turn lane, 9-11 parking spaces added.

corridors.name: Commerce Drive (east)
corridors.ext: Clairemont Ave to E College Ave
corridors.today: 4 lanes, measured speeds 36-40 mph, bike lanes end at Church St
corridors.proposal: Road diet with one-way protected bike lanes. Protected intersection at N Candler St, where a serious bike crash happened in 2022. Add speed management on the curves.
corridors.impactNote: 12,500-13,000 vehicles/day is well under road-diet thresholds. Speeds of 36-40 mph, not capacity, are the problem here.
corridors.serves: Recreation Center, Talley St Upper ES, Glennwood ES, E College Ave
corridors.src: Safety Action Plan 2025; PATH #1 built only west of Church St
corridors.city: Calls this the HIN segment with the most crashes and no project. Says a road diet is "an appropriate change." No bike facility is specified east of Church St.
corridors.change: Adds one-way protected bike lanes to the road diet, plus a protected intersection at N Candler St.

corridors.name: S McDonough St - Oakview Rd spine
corridors.ext: W College Ave to Oakhurst Village
corridors.today: 2 lanes, traffic calming at College Heights, no bike facility
corridors.proposal: Build the Oakview / S McDonough PATH project as a two-way protected bikeway, with on-street parking kept on the opposite side. Include a protected crossing at the railroad and W College Ave.
corridors.impactNote: Volumes are low, so this needs no lane reduction. The space comes from lane narrowing and putting parking on one side.
corridors.serves: Decatur HS, Beacon Hill MS, College Heights ECLC, Oakhurst ES, Oakhurst Village, McKoy Park
corridors.src: PATH plan #2 Agnes Scott Connector and #3 Oakview Rd Connector (2016); Safety Action Plan
corridors.city: A two-way cycle track across the tracks on S McDonough, then a 10-ft side path through the Agnes Scott campus to E Davis St, then the Oakview Rd trail west to Oakhurst Village.
corridors.change: Keeps the Oakview design. Offers an on-street S McDonough route for the middle section in case the campus route (which needs Agnes Scott's agreement) stalls.

corridors.name: West College Avenue
corridors.ext: East Lake MARTA to S McDonough St
corridors.today: Wide lanes, painted bike lanes on parts
corridors.proposal: Lane diet (10-11 ft lanes) to free space for curb-separated or post-protected bike lanes, as the Safety Action Plan recommends. Upgrade Atlanta Ave and S McDonough St to protected intersections.
corridors.impactNote: Lanes get narrower but none are removed.
corridors.serves: Beacon Hill MS, East Lake MARTA, downtown
corridors.city: Extend bikeways east from the city limit and East Lake MARTA, with a lane diet and school-zone speed cameras near Beacon Hill MS.
corridors.change: Specifies curb or post protection and protected intersections at Atlanta Ave and S McDonough St.

corridors.name: East College Avenue
corridors.ext: S McDonough St to city limit (Avondale)
corridors.today: 4-5 lanes, 35 mph, most bike crashes of any Decatur street (6)
corridors.proposal: Back GDOT PI 0018335 (road diet + protected bike lane from the east city limit to S Candler St) and extend it west to S McDonough St. Protected intersection at Commerce Dr, which had 3 bike crashes.
corridors.impactNote: At ~28,000 vehicles/day a lane reduction needs GDOT corridor modeling. GDOT has already programmed it on the eastern segment.
corridors.serves: Agnes Scott College, Winnona Park ES, Talley St Upper ES, Avondale MARTA
corridors.city: GDOT has programmed a road diet with a protected bike lane from the east city limit west to S Candler St. The Safety Action Plan recommends a protected bikeway along the whole corridor.
corridors.change: Extends GDOT's project west from S Candler St to S McDonough St and adds a protected intersection at Commerce Dr.

corridors.name: West Ponce de Leon Avenue
corridors.ext: W Trinity Pl to Scott Blvd roundabout
corridors.today: Painted bike lanes outside parking; bike lane drops at W Trinity Pl
corridors.proposal: Pick Alternative 2 from the city's 2026 study: swap parking and bike lanes to make parking-protected lanes with a 3-ft door buffer. Close the gap at W Trinity Pl with a protected merge, which had 2 bike crashes including 1 serious.
corridors.impactNote: Keeps all lanes and most parking. Narrower lanes slow traffic.
corridors.serves: St. Thomas More, Adair Park, downtown, Druid Hills
corridors.src: W Ponce de Leon Ave Safety Improvements (2026 study)
corridors.city: Alternative 1 removes south-side parking to widen the bike lanes. Alternative 2 swaps parking and bike lanes to make parking-protected lanes.
corridors.change: Picks Alternative 2 and adds a fix for the bike-lane drop at W Trinity Pl, which the community flagged.

corridors.name: East Ponce de Leon Avenue
corridors.proposal: Corridor study, as the Safety Action Plan calls for. Preferred option: 4-to-3 conversion with protected lanes. Fallback: a two-way sidepath on the south side. Phase 1 builds the Glennwood greenway as a parallel low-stress route.
corridors.impactNote: Close to the upper range for a road diet. Modeling should come first.
corridors.serves: Glennwood ES, Avondale MARTA, Stone Mountain Trail
corridors.city: Provide a bikeway between Avondale MARTA and downtown, plus speed management.
corridors.change: Frames it as a study first (4-to-3 preferred, south-side path as fallback) and adds a parallel greenway in Phase 1.

corridors.name: Scott Boulevard shared-use path
corridors.ext: W Ponce de Leon Ave to N Decatur Rd
corridors.today: 4 lanes undivided, 40 mph, the most dangerous road in Decatur
corridors.proposal: Shared-use path and planted median through the RAISE planning grant. Roundabouts or protected intersections at Clairemont Ave and W Ponce de Leon Ave.
corridors.impactNote: The path goes behind the curb, so no lanes are removed. A median and roundabouts slow traffic without cutting capacity.
corridors.serves: Westchester ES, Clairemont ES, Emory/Druid Hills
corridors.src: RAISE planning grant ($1.87M); Safety Action Plan; GDOT PI 0015682 roundabout
corridors.city: Shared-use path, tree-lined median, more mid-block crossings, roundabouts or protected intersections.

corridors.name: East Lake Drive
corridors.ext: W College Ave (East Lake MARTA) to 2nd Ave
corridors.today: Painted bike lanes in places; repaving project under way
corridors.proposal: Use the 2026 repaving (Park Pl to 2nd Ave) and extend north to W College Ave to upgrade to buffered lanes with flex posts or curb stops. Raised crossings at Oakhurst ES and Spring St, where there was a 2023 bike crash.
corridors.impactNote: The repaving restripes the street anyway, and no lanes are removed.
corridors.serves: Oakhurst ES, Oakhurst Village, East Lake
corridors.city: Repaving with safety upgrades, Park Pl to 2nd Ave only.
corridors.change: Extends north to W College Ave and East Lake MARTA and adds flex posts and raised school crossings.

corridors.name: E Trinity Pl / E Howard Ave connector
corridors.ext: N McDonough St to Talley St Upper ES
corridors.today: Downtown couplet; E Howard/E Trinity had 2 bike crashes (1 serious)
corridors.proposal: One-way protected lanes on E Trinity Pl, a protected intersection at E Howard Ave, and a two-way bikeway on E Howard Ave along the railroad to Agnes Scott.
corridors.impactNote: Reallocates lane width. E Howard carries low volume.
corridors.serves: Decatur HS, Agnes Scott College (via S Candler St), Talley St Upper ES
corridors.city: E Trinity Pl is on the High Injury Network, and residents flagged E Howard/E Trinity for sight-line problems. No bikeway has been proposed.
corridors.change: New protected link from downtown east along the railroad to Agnes Scott and Talley St Upper ES.

corridors.name: West Side Connector
corridors.owner: City (CSX and GDOT at the crossing)
corridors.today: No continuous north-south route west of downtown. The railroad and W College Ave block it, and the Atlanta Ave crossing area had 3 bike crashes.
corridors.proposal: A north-south spine for west Decatur. North of W Ponce it uses the Scott Blvd path (C9) and W Ponce lanes (C7). From the W Ponce/W Trinity merge it runs south as a traffic-calmed greenway on Adair St, past St. Thomas More and Adair Park, to the W Howard cycle track and Stone Mountain Trail. It crosses the CSX tracks at the new Adair St crossing in the city's approved 2019 concept, crosses W College Ave at the new signal, and continues as a greenway on Mead Rd past Oakhurst ES to Oakhurst Village, where it meets the Oakview spine (C4).
corridors.impactNote: Adair St and Mead Rd carry low volumes. The rail crossing and W College signal are already in the city concept. Traffic calming on Adair was funded in 2021-22.
corridors.serves: Westchester ES, St. Thomas More, Adair Park, Ebster Park, W Howard cycle track, Beacon Hill MS (via W College), Oakhurst ES, Oakhurst Village, East Lake MARTA (via PATH #7)
corridors.src: Not in any city plan; it connects PATH #6, the 2019 Adair St rail-crossing concept, and PATH #3/#7
corridors.city: Separate pieces exist: PATH #6 (Westchester ES trail), the approved Adair St rail-crossing concept with a new W College signal, a funded Adair St traffic-calming plan, and PATH #7 (East Lake MARTA greenway). Nothing joins them into a north-south route.
corridors.change: New route that ties these pieces into one continuous west-side spine.

greenways.name: North Schools Greenway
greenways.city: A trail from Glenlake Park through Decatur Cemetery to Glennwood ES. It needs some land acquisition.
greenways.change: Adds an on-street greenway from Clairemont ES to Glennwood ES that needs no land. The cemetery trail stays the long-term goal.

greenways.name: South Schools Greenway
greenways.src: Safety Action Plan (general Safe Routes to School policy)
greenways.city: The plan calls for neighborhood greenways in general but names no route.
greenways.change: New school-to-school route linking Oakhurst ES, College Heights and Winnona Park ES.

greenways.name: Winnona - Legacy Park Greenway
greenways.change: New route from Winnona Park ES to Columbia Seminary and Legacy Park.

greenways.name: Glennwood - Recreation Center Greenway
greenways.src: PATH plan #5 Glennwood Elementary Connector (south end)
greenways.city: A greenway on Sycamore Pl from Glennwood ES to the Stone Mountain Trail.
greenways.change: No change. Extended to the Recreation Center and library.

greenways.name: Westside Greenway
greenways.src: Safety Action Plan (Electric Ave speed management)
greenways.city: Speed management on Electric Ave near the school recreation facility. No bike route named.
greenways.change: New greenway from St. Thomas More and Ebster Park to Decatur HS.

greenways.name: East Decatur Greenway (PATH #4)
greenways.city: A Shoal Creek trail to Dearborn Park, with a greenway on Midway Rd and Oldfield Rd to Kirk Rd.
greenways.change: No change. Only the street greenway is drawn; the creek trail needs field alignment.

carried.d: Paved trails in Hidden Cove Park, the Scott Blvd HAWK crossing, and a creek trail to Garden Ln. Carried forward as a quieter long-term alternative to the Scott Blvd path for the north end of the West Side Connector.

A neighborhood greenway on Winter Ave, Madison Ave and 1st Ave to Oakview Rd. Carried forward unchanged. It extends the West Side Connector to East Lake MARTA. Not drawn because Winter Ave is missing from the street data.
The Shoal Creek trail to Dearborn Park. Carried forward unchanged; only its street greenway is drawn (G7).
The Safety Action Plan prohibits right turns on red at 12 downtown intersections. Supported, and extended to every protected intersection in this proposal.

issues: Six walking and biking crashes involved a driver turning left who did not yield to someone in the crosswalk or to an oncoming rider.
One driver ran a red light and seriously injured a pedestrian in the crosswalk.
A right-turning driver struck the school crossing guard and left. Two of the walking and biking crashes were hit-and-runs.
More crashes of all kinds than any other site on this list.
